pairs.why: B's plain glossy dome and clean rim match the simple, readable forms of the real cards, while A's printed cross on the dome is an extra detail the real cards would not add.
A's plain dome and clean hull read simpler and closer to the real submarine and lamp, while B adds an odd cross emblem.
The two saucers are nearly the same in finish, color and build, and differ only by a few rivets and the size of the lights.
A has fewer surface screws and a cleaner, smoother hull, closer to the lightly detailed real cards, while B adds busier rivet clutter.
A's foil is softer, with smoother broad wrinkles, closer to the smooth-but-not-plastic real finish, while B's crinkles are sharper and more texture-heavy.
A has gentler, rounder folds and a cleaner silhouette, while B's crumpled foil reads as more texture-heavy than the real cards.
A's surface is smoother with fewer fine creases, in line with the lessons' preference for less texture, while B shows busier crinkling.
A's broad, soft wrinkles feel closer to the smooth stylized real cards than B's denser crinkled foil.
